## Reasoning effort

A reasoning effort is a **saved setting on a m
odel selection**, not a free-standing\nfield. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `source`, an optional `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallba

ck`) carries it as `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is
accepted everywhere a model choice is saved:

| Where | Fi
eld |\n| - | - |\n| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.modelSelection` (or `config.modelSelection` on
a whole-config replacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure-adhoc`) | `modelSelection`, read back on t
he environment |\n| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`, read back on the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /p
rojects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`, read back on the suite |\n\n```json theme={\"theme
m`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of\n them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEfforts` on each row of the public\n `GET /v1/
models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n that model; do not guess one.\n* **Applied or refused,
never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded on the execution record, or refused with\n
`capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling\n temperature.\n* **A selection belongs to one model.** It
must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins its own model. A bare model\n change
on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model\n instead of failing.\n* **Cases keep their selections.** A
`models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's existing selection for that\n model. S
end `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a client `set`, an environment\n or a suite
, keeping the bare model id.\n* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an unknown key\n (`apiKey`, …) is a `400
`.\n* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`\n reports `modelSelections`; an older deployment
rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied, so\n writing it is a `400` pointing

at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored
 value is refused by the runner.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-le
vel `reasoningEffort` for a\nper-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the session's **first\nturn** (a continuation
that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved selection carries, and it cannot be combined with `temp

erature`.

The SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operations:
`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a sho

rthand that edits the selection the target
already has, and is refused (`send modelSelection`) when there is none.

## Not in t

he API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** available over the API
today (most exist in the hosted insp

ector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design; see [Authentication](#authentication))
* Chat and conformance s
uites\n* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth yourself,\n then upload the token to one of the server's

[accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z); it directly sha

pes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general
\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **During the preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still ha
ppen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).\n* **Additive changes** (new endpoints
, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes) are considered non-breaking and can ship\n at any time. W

rite clients that ignore unknown fields.
* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed sur

faces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is
**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave

` is **swarm run**. The paths, the
operation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |

| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |
| `/projects/{pro
jectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environme
nts/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/p
rojects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}
` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projec
ts/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` |\n\nResponse fields followed t
heir nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →\n`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.\n\
nTwo reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and\n`get_user_testing_scenario` served the environment id and
the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are\nabsent rather than null when you may n

ot have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including its old response
spellings. Each one answers with `De
precation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. The old paths are not in the OpenAPI spec, and they are removed\nat ge

neral availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the rename and so have no
deprecated twin to hold the old
field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either, never both in\none reques

t, until general availability.

### Vocabulary

Renamed field values cannot be aliased the way paths are, so they are chosen

by header. Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read
canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |\
n| - | - | - |\n| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |\n| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`,
`goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| s
hare `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |\n\nAbsent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract
. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vo

cabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

Th
is is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is\neval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deploy

ment may speak one
and not the other, so read
`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` (`apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are
tw
o blocks) before sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or\n`client.withApiVocabulary(2)

` on one you already hold.

Permalink resource types work differently: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_tes
ting_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION rather
than the header; a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.res

ourceTypes`
lists both.
